1.

This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act')
has been filed by the claimant challenging the judgment dated 03.08.2021 passed by MACT No.XV,
Vijayapura in MVC No.1015/2017.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeal briefly stated are that on 04.12.2017 when the claimant was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28- EP-4336 as a pillion rider on Vijayapura-Kolhar Road near Dadamatti cross, at that time, Sikandar, rider of the said motorcycle rode the same at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, being unable to control, turtled down in a ditch and caused accident.
As a result of the aforesaid accident, the claimant sustained grievous injuries and was hospitalized.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7404-DB HC-KAR 3.
The claimant filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act, seeking compensation.
It was pleaded that she spent significant amount towards medical expenses, conveyance charges and other related costs.
It was further pleaded that the accident occurred solely on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.2 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.
The respondent No.1, despite service of notice, did not appear before the Tribunal and was placed ex-parte.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.
The Tribunal, by impugned judgment and award has dismissed the claim petition.
Being aggrieved, the present appeal has been filed.

sentences.text: 3 6. Learned counsel for the claimant has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28-EP-4336.
Immediately after that accident, the claimant has been admitted to Yashodhara Hospital, Vijayapura.

As per the medical records, it is clearly mentioned that the claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident case due to negligence of the rider of the motorcycle and skid of the motorcycle, as a result of which, the claimant has suffered injuries.
Even the police after thorough investigation have filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle.
Only because there is delay in lodging the complaint, the Tribunal has rejected the claim petition.
He further contented that the claimant was admitted in the hospital and her husband was taking care of her.
Therefore, they were not able to give complaint immediately.
After 4 days from the date of accident, her husband lodged a complaint.
The Tribunal without considering this aspect of NC: 2025:KHC-K:7404-DB HC-KAR the matter has erred in dismissing the claim petition.
Hence, he sought for allowing the appeal.
7. Learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contented that there is delay in lodging the complaint.
In the complaint, they have specifically stated that the rider of the motorcycle was riding the same in a rash and negligent manner and motorcycle turned turtle.
In the IMV report, there is no damage to the motorcycle and the rider has not suffered any injuries.
Therefore, it is very clear that to make a false claim, the claimant has implicated the motorcycle.
The Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim petition.
Hence, he sought for dismissal of the appeal.

8. Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.
9.

The case of the claimants is that on 04.12.2017 when the claimant was proceeding on motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28-EP-4336 as a pillion rider on Vijayapura-Kolhar Road near Dadamatti cross, at that NC: 2025:KHC-K:7404-DB HC-KAR time, Sikander, rider of the said motorcycle rode the same at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner, unable to control,
turtle down in a ditch and caused accident.
Due to said impact, claimant sustained injuries.
Immediately after that accident, she has been shifted to Yashodhara Hospital, Vijayapura.
10. In the medical records produced before the court, it is mentioned that it is a RTA case and accident has occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the motorcycle.
The specific case of the claimant is that she has suffered serious injuries in the said accident and she was shifted to hospital and admitted on the same day and discharged on 13.12.2017.
Therefore, she could not lodge the complaint immediately.
To prove the case, the claimant has examined herself as PW1.
The FIR has been lodged against the rider of the motorcycle.
Police have filed chare sheet against the rider of the motorcycle.

In the wound certificate, it is mentioned as 'history of fall from two wheeler bike and rider did not fall, head injury'.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7404-DB HC-KAR
The Tribunal, without considering all these aspects, only on the ground that there is a delay in lodging the complaint, has dismissed the claim petition.

To disprove the case of the claimant, the respondent-Insurance Company has not examined any witnesses, neither the Investigation Officer has been examined nor the rider of the motorcycle has been examined, and they have not elicited any worthwhile information from the evidence of PW1 in the cross examination.

sentences.text: Under these circumstances, we are of the opinion that in order to give one more opportunity to the parties, the matter requires to be remitted back to the Tribunal for fresh consideration.

12. In the result, following order is passed:
ORDER a) Appeal is allowed.
b) The judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is set aside.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:7404-DB HC-KAR c) Matter is remitted back to the Tribunal for fresh consideration, reserving liberty to the parties to adduce additional evidence and produce additional documents.
d) Tribunal after hearing the parties shall pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, without being influenced by any observation made by this Court in this order.
e) Registry is directed to return the original records to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
